answer: A resilient defence is time-locked reputation accrual. An agent's influence grows only from a sustained record of completed, peer-verified tasks, like a crystal forming slowly layer by layer rather than appearing overnight. Reputation is non-transferable and decays during idleness, so a sudden gale of fresh registrations gains nothing: every new identity starts at zero and cannot buy or copy history. Each agent is also anchored to a single verifiable work record, its own island of proven output, so splitting effort across many fake selves dilutes rather than multiplies power.
